answer.method: Utility rows from Heimdall Storm Blackout v1.2 (data__utility_by_county.csv) were kept when declared = true, available = true, peak_customers_out is present, customers_total > 0, and peak_customers_out / customers_total >= 0.10. A county-storm qualified on duration when hours_to_90pct_restored > 72, or when it is empty with reason not_restored_in_window (never restored within the window). Eta was counted once: DR-4588 rows were mapped to AL292020. Hospitals came from HIFLD Next hospitals-3 v1.1.0 (geoparquet), limited to STATUS = OPEN and joined on COUNTYFIPS = geoid (5-digit text). Pairs are distinct (source_ID, storm). Storms are distinct storms with at least one qualifying county (241); 211 of those storms have at least one qualifying hospital county. Trauma counts are hospitals with at least one qualifying storm, grouped by the TRAUMA field as recorded.
caveats: Rows with hours_to_90pct_reason reporting_drop or peak_mismatch have no restoration time and were excluded, even if their peak share was at least 10%; the feed-stop cases could hide qualifying counties.
Customer totals are EIA-861 estimates split by housing units, so the 10% share is approximate.
The 90% threshold uses the 45-day window, so 'not restored' means not restored within 45 days (or until the next FEMA storm in the county), not never restored.
Eta has two records (AL292020 and DR-4588) with different county values; I counted it once by mapping DR-4588 to AL292020. Using both records would change the counts.
Storms count is 241 by county, but only 211 storms have a hospital in a qualifying county.
The top-10 list has ties: the 9th-10th IDs and several others have 4 storms each, so the cut at 10 is arbitrary; two more hospitals (0012732117, 0015132114) also have 4.
Hospital county assignment uses HIFLD COUNTYFIPS, not geocoding; the Connecticut county change and Bedford city (51515) are not handled.
Most hospitals (1,679 of 2,283) have trauma status 'NOT AVAILABLE', and the TRAUMA field mixes levels, categories and pediatric/adult designations, so the trauma breakdown is not a clean level count.
The 'more than once' count uses storm groups, so Eta contributes at most one storm per hospital.
Night-light fields are not used; the analysis relies on EAGLE-I utility records only, and EAGLE-I coverage is incomplete in some years and states.
